title: G Major Scale
description: Your first scale with a black key in it. G major is all white keys except one: F#.

steps.title: One sharp
steps.description: G major uses the same pattern of steps as C major (whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half), just starting on G. To make that pattern fit, F gets raised to F# (F sharp). So the notes are G, A, B, C, D, E, F#. Everything else stays on the white keys.

steps.title: Find G
steps.description: Press G4. Look for a group of three black keys. G is the white key between the first and second of them.
steps.hint: From middle C, G is five white keys up, counting C as one.

steps.title: Find F#
steps.description: F# is the black key between F and G. Press any F# you like. It's the one note that makes G major different from C major.
steps.hint: Look for the first black key in a group of three, just below G.

steps.title: Now the whole scale
steps.description: Play up from G: G, A, B, C, D, E, F#. Seven notes, and only the last one is a black key. Any octave works.
steps.hint: Play white keys all the way up, but when you get to F, use the black key just above it instead.

steps.title: The G major chord
steps.description: Finish with the G major chord: G, B and D together. It's the home chord of this scale.
steps.hint: Thumb on G, middle finger on B, pinky on D.

steps.title: Which one's sharp?
steps.description: In the G major scale, which note gets a sharp?
